reason: Para 7 states verbatim that the demand of the imitatio Christi 'ought logically to have the result of developing and exalting the inner man'; the relation preserves Jung's crucial hedge ('ought logically'), which the paragraph immediately counters with 'In actual fact, however' — so the hedged relation is the only correct reading, and it is kept.

Para 12 asserts this both in the quoted sentence ('it is all veneer, but the inner man has remained untouched and therefore unchanged') and independently ('a psychic condition that has remained archaic and has not been even remotely touched by Christianity'; 'Christ only meets them from without, never from within the soul'), so attributing the claim to the christianity node, not just 'Christian civilization', is warranted by the whole paragraph.

Para 11 argues the soul 'must contain in itself the faculty of relationship to God, i.e., a correspondence' and then states 'This correspondence is, in psychological terms, the archetype of the God-image'; the ellipsis splices two sentences whose identity Jung himself asserts, so the quote is not misleading and the direction (soul contains the archetype) is correct.

Para 13 states verbatim that 'the mysterium magnum is not only an actuality but is first and foremost rooted in the human psyche' (framed as something that 'has yet to be understood', i.e. Jung asserting it as fact); direction and claim_type correct.

Para 14 states verbatim 'the soul is naturaliter religiosa, i.e., possesses a religious function', which Jung explicitly claims to have proved from facts ('I did not attribute a religious function to the soul, I merely produced the facts'); jung-asserts is correct.

Para 15: 'when I say as a psychologist that God is an archetype, I mean by that the “type” in the psyche' — mapping the subject to god-image rather than God correctly captures Jung's own restriction to the psychic imprint (he expressly refuses any metaphysical assertion about God in the same paragraph).

Para 20 opens verbatim: 'The archetypes of the unconscious can be shown empirically to be the equivalents of religious dogmas'; the relation name preserves the empirical qualifier and the paragraph is about religious dogma generally, matching the dogma node.

Para 22 states verbatim 'The self is a union of opposites par excellence, and this is where it differs essentially from the Christ-symbol' (Christ 'simply represents good, and his counterpart the devil, evil'); the christ node in this graph denotes the symbolic figure Jung discusses throughout the paragraph, and direction is correct.

Para 24 opens verbatim: 'Without the experience of the opposites there is no experience of wholeness'; the relation keeps 'experience-of' on the object side and correctly renders the opposites as the precondition.

Para 26: 'just as the dream compensates the conflicts of the conscious mind, so alchemy endeavours to fill in the gaps left open by the Christian tension of opposites', with alchemy described as 'an undercurrent to the Christianity that ruled on the surface'; the hedge 'endeavours' is preserved in the relation and the compensation framing is Jung's own analogy in the same sentence.

Para 26 states the even numbers 'are personified by the serpens mercurii, the dragon that creates and destroys itself and represents the prima materia'; this is Jung expounding alchemical doctrine, so jung-reports-parallel (not jung-asserts) is the correct type.
Para 30 states verbatim 'The essence of the conscious mind is discrimination; it must, if it is to be aware of things, separate the opposites'; subject, direction, and claim_type all correct.

Para 30: in the unconscious 'and particularly in the archetype of unity, the self. Here, as in the deity, the opposites cancel out' — the paragraph asserts exactly that the opposites cancel out in the self; quote accurate.

Para 36 describes the shadow as 'that dark half of the psyche which we invariably get rid of by means of projection' (either onto neighbours or onto a divine mediator); the relation matches Jung's 'get rid of by means of' and the direction is correct.

Para 38 states verbatim that 'the contents of the personal unconscious (i.e., the shadow) are indistinguishably merged with the archetypal contents of the collective unconscious'; the edge compresses 'archetypal contents of the collective unconscious' to the collective-unconscious node, which the paragraph's point (the shadow drags those contents up with it) supports.

Para 40 states 'alchemy and astrology were ceaselessly engaged in preserving the bridge to nature, i.e., to the unconscious psyche, from decay'; alchemy is one of the two named subjects, so the edge is fully licensed (astrology's parallel role is omitted, not misrepresented).

Para 40 closes verbatim: 'What the symbolism of alchemy expresses is the whole problem of the evolution of personality described above, the so-called individuation process'; alchemy-expresses-individuation is a faithful compression since it is alchemy's own symbolism doing the expressing.

Para 41 describes individuals 'possessed by archetypes of a numinous nature that force their way to the surface in order to form new dominants' when 'the collective dominants of human life fall into decay', with Christianity given as the worked example; the edge matches the paragraph's claim and direction.

Para 44 states verbatim 'I call this centre the “self,” which should be understood as the totality of the psyche', reinforced by the next sentence ('not only the centre, but also the whole circumference which embraces both conscious and unconscious').

Para 57 opens verbatim: 'The sea is the symbol of the collective unconscious, because unfathomed depths lie concealed beneath its reflecting surface'; this is Jung's own interpretive assertion in the dream commentary, so jung-asserts is correct.
